answer: To secure an AI agent economy against Sybil attacks, networks can employ cryptographic resource bonding requiring every autonomous node to prove computational work by decrypting a unique time-locked cipher using hardware enclaves. If a malicious entity attempts to spawn fake identities, the verification process forces them to burn a verifiable cryptographic ember of computational proof of stake for each instance. This economic friction acts as a digital lantern, illuminating illegitimate nodes and making mass replication economically unviable.
